title: Physics lab — slow-mo throw & pendulum
blurb: Measures gravity from a thrown ball, a pendulum's swing, occlusion bridging, slow-motion timing.

tour.title: A finished analysis
tour.text: This clip was filmed in slow motion at 240 fps: a ball is thrown and a pendulum swings. Everything is already tracked and measured. Press Space to play it (and again to pause). Use Next to walk through what's here.

tour.title: Slow-motion: real time
tour.text: The file plays at 30 fps but was recorded at 240 fps. Capture rate (right panel, Time & filtering) is set to 240 so seconds and speeds are real — otherwise every speed would be 8× too slow. Set this whenever you use a phone's slow-mo mode.

tour.title: Scale & origin
tour.text:
The yellow line on the metre stick is the scale: 300 pixels = 1.00 m. The arrows are the axes: (0, 0) is where the ball was thrown from, x (red) is metres to the right, y (green) is metres up. So the ball's y is its height above the launch point.
Try it: drag a yellow end of the line — every number updates. Ctrl+Z puts it back.

tour.title: The ball's path
tour.text: The orange trail is the ball's path. The graph below shows its height over time — a parabola. Hover the graph to read values; click it to jump the video to that moment.

tour.title: Measuring gravity
tour.text: This is the ball's vertical speed. While it flies it falls in a straight line — the slope is gravity. Hover two points on the line: it drops about 9.8 m/s every second. The jumps are the bounces.

tour.title: Hidden behind the post
tour.text: For frames 91–107 the ball is behind the post. The tracker coasted along the predicted path and picked it up again on the other side. Those frames are left empty (see the gap in the orange lane on the timeline) rather than made up. Edit → Fill gaps can interpolate them.

tour.title: Lost: left the picture
tour.text: At frame 311 the ball rolls out of the picture, so the tracker stops — marked red on the timeline and "last seen here" on the video. If a point is lost while it's still visible, just click where it is (or press Enter to take the dashed guess) and tracking carries on.

tour.title: A fixed point
tour.text: Pivot is a fixed point (square marker): it never moves, so it isn't tracked — see "Fixed point" ticked in the point settings. Use fixed points for anything stationary you want to measure against.

tour.title: Pendulum angle
tour.text: Pendulum angle is a tilt measurement: the angle of the Pivot→Bob line against the x-axis, so hanging straight down is −90°. It swings between about −64° and −116° — a smooth wave on the graph. Measurements are listed under Measurements; untick one to hide it.

tour.title: String length
tour.text: String length is a distance measurement. It stays at 0.60 m the whole time — a good sanity check that the tracking and scale are right. Live values for the current frame are in At this frame.

tour.title: Smoothing
tour.text: Speeds and accelerations come from differentiating positions, which amplifies jitter, so the app applies a zero-lag low-pass filter (Smoothing: Auto). Flying, the ball's acceleration reads ≈ 9.8 m/s² — gravity again.

tour.title: Playback speed & loops
tour.text: The bar under the video: ◀ / ▶| step one frame (or the ← → keys; Shift for 10), the 1× box changes playback speed, and [ ] set a range. A range is set now (frames 0–200, shaded blue on the timeline): playback loops inside it and tracking stops at its ends. ✕ (or \) clears it.

tour.title: Get the numbers out
tour.text: Export CSV (Ctrl+E) saves every frame's positions, speeds and measurements as a spreadsheet. Export video renders the clip with all these overlays. That's the tour — open your own video from File → Open, or try another example from Help → Examples.
